prompt: I'm seeing some odd "clean start" behavior in SFTPGo from this checkout as I get ready to run it behind a TLS terminating reverse proxy, and I want to understand what the service is actually doing at runtime. When I start it with a temporary config directory and then hit a few obvious endpoints like `/`, `/web`, `/metrics`, and a couple of missing paths, some things seem to shift between runs in ways that don't match what my teammate expects. They're convinced a temp config directory isolates everything and that it should not matter whether I start the process from the repo root or some other folder, but the symptoms make it feel like the process is quietly finding state or defaults from somewhere else. Can you help me narrow down what is really happening by comparing a few "first start" situations, like SQLite missing versus empty versus already usable, the SFTP port already being taken, and the web UI assets not being where the server expects, and then telling me what changes in startup behavior, exit status, and the HTTP responses that come back? I'm also confused about the proxy header story: when requests include `Forwarded` and the usual `X-Forwarded-For` and `X-Real-IP`, which address and scheme does SFTPGo actually log, what happens when there are multiple IPs in a forwarded chain, and does the working directory affect any of that? I'd like to see a couple of short snippets that make the behavior undeniable, like a few relevant startup log lines, a small slice of the HTTP response headers for those endpoints, one representative access log line for a request with proxy style headers (you can redact volatile fields like timestamps and request IDs), and the specific `/metrics` lines that show how the `sftpgo_http` counters move when you repeat the same request with and without forwarded headers. Temporary scripts may be used for observation, but the repository itself should remain unchanged and anything temporary should be cleaned up afterward.

reference_answer:
I built and ran SFTPGo from this checkout and I only trusted what I could observe in stdout logs, HTTP responses, the structured access log lines, and /metrics.
I built the binary and ran it with serve while pointing at a brand new temp config directory each time.

cd /appgo build -o /tmp/sftpgo ./

When I ran it from /app with an empty temp config directory and no database file, it did not bootstrap SQLite and it failed immediately during data provider init, but the process exit code was still zero.
EC=0{"level":"debug","sender":"config","message":"config file used: '/app/sftpgo.json', ..."}{"level":"warn","sender":"sqlite","message":"sqlite database file does not exists, please be sure to create and initialize a database before starting sftpgo"}{"level":"error","sender":"service","message":"error initializing data provider: stat /tmp/.../sftpgo.db: no such file or directory"}

When I repeated that with a zero byte sftpgo.db file present, it still did not initialize anything and it failed with the “invalid” message, and it still exited zero.
EC=0{"level":"debug","sender":"config","message":"config file used: '/app/sftpgo.json', ..."}{"level":"error","sender":"service","message":"error initializing data provider: sqlite database file is invalid, please be sure to create and initialize a database before starting sftpgo"}

When I created a real SQLite DB file by applying the repo’s sqlite SQL migrations into $CONF_DIR/sftpgo.db and I also copied templates and static into the temp config directory, the run came up and I saw it open the SQLite handle and start HTTP and SFTP.
{"level":"debug","sender":"sqlite","message":"sqlite database handle created, connection string: \"file:/tmp/.../sftpgo.db?cache=shared\""}{"level":"debug","sender":"httpd","message":"initializing HTTP server with config {BindPort:8080 BindAddress:127.0.0.1 ...}"}{"level":"info","sender":"sftpd","message":"server listener registered address: [::]:2022"}

That “working” run still left new files behind in the temp config directory, even though I started from a fresh directory. The main surprise was that it generated an SSH host key.
id_rsasftpgo.dbstatic/...templates/...backups/...

I also tested the teammate claim about the temp config dir always isolating config and never reading from the current working directory. When I launched from /app I kept seeing config file used: '/app/sftpgo.json' even though my temp config dir did not contain a config file. When I launched from /tmp with the same idea, config load failed and it fell back to defaults, which showed up in the startup log.
{"level":"warn","sender":"config","message":"error loading configuration file: Unsupported Config Type \"\". Default configuration will be used: {...}"}
On the web side, I kept the healthy instance running and hit endpoints with curl. / and /web were not 200. Both were redirects to /web/users.
GET /HTTP/1.1 301 Moved PermanentlyLocation: /web/usersGET /webHTTP/1.1 301 Moved PermanentlyLocation: /web/users
/web/users returned HTML 200 and looked like the UI entry point.
HTTP/1.1 200 OKContent-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en">
A totally non existent route like /nope came back as JSON 404, and /web/nope was also JSON 404, not HTML.
HTTP/1.1 404 Not FoundContent-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8{"error":"","message":"Not Found","status":404}
A “real route with a missing record” behaved differently. /web/user/1 returned a 404 with an HTML error page and the title showed it was a web template response.
HTTP/1.1 404 Not FoundContent-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8<title>SFTPGo - Not found</title>
A missing static asset behaved differently again. /static/nope returned plain text 404.
HTTP/1.1 404 Not FoundContent-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8404 page not found
The REST API was not locked down by default in this build. I could hit it without any auth and get real responses.
GET /api/v1/userHTTP/1.1 200 OK[]GET /api/v1/versionHTTP/1.1 200 OK{"version":"0.9.5-dev","build_date":"","commit_hash":""}
Method not allowed was also a JSON response.
POST /api/v1/versionHTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed{"error":"","message":"Method not allowed","status":405}
A missing API record returned JSON 404 with an error field populated.
GET /api/v1/user/1HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found{"error":"Not found: sql: no rows in result set","message":"","status":404}

I then exercised the proxy header story by sending the same GET / request plain and then again with Forwarded, X-Forwarded-For, and X-Real-IP. The HTTP response did not change between plain and proxy-ish. Both came back as the same 301 redirect with the same Location.
plain GET /HTTP/1.1 301 Moved PermanentlyLocation: /web/usersproxy-ish GET /HTTP/1.1 301 Moved PermanentlyLocation: /web/users

What changed was what got logged. Here are the two access-log lines (volatile values redacted) for those two requests. The plain request logged remote_addr as the real socket address with a port and logged uri under 127.0.0.1:8080. The proxy-ish request logged remote_addr as the first IP in X-Forwarded-For and logged uri with the Host header I set.
{"level":"info","time":"[REDACTED]","sender":"httpd","method":"GET","proto":"HTTP/1.1","remote_addr":"127.0.0.1:45324","request_id":"[REDACTED]","uri":"http://127.0.0.1:8080/","user_agent":"curl/8.12.1","resp_status":301,"resp_size":45,"elapsed_ms":0}{"level":"info","time":"[REDACTED]","sender":"httpd","method":"GET","proto":"HTTP/1.1","remote_addr":"203.0.113.9","request_id":"[REDACTED]","uri":"http://hosthdr.example/","user_agent":"curl/8.12.1","resp_status":301,"resp_size":45,"elapsed_ms":0}
That proxy-ish line also answers the “which address and scheme does it log” question. With X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.9, 10.0.0.1 and X-Real-IP: 198.51.100.7, the logged remote_addr matched the first X-Forwarded-For IP, not X-Real-IP and not the last forwarded-for IP. And even though I sent X-Forwarded-Proto: https and Forwarded: proto=https, the logged uri still started with http://, so those proto headers did not flip the logged scheme to https:// in this setup.

I also checked how the sftpgo_http_* metrics move when repeating the same request plain versus with forwarded headers. I took a /metrics snapshot, then did a plain GET /, then took another snapshot, then did the proxy-ish GET /, then took a third snapshot. These are the exact /metrics lines I captured each time.
/metrics snapshot before the plain GET /sftpgo_http_client_errors_total 0sftpgo_http_req_ok_total 1sftpgo_http_req_total 1sftpgo_http_server_errors_total 0/metrics snapshot after the plain GET /sftpgo_http_client_errors_total 0sftpgo_http_req_ok_total 2sftpgo_http_req_total 3sftpgo_http_server_errors_total 0/metrics snapshot after the proxy-ish GET /sftpgo_http_client_errors_total 0sftpgo_http_req_ok_total 3sftpgo_http_req_total 5sftpgo_http_server_errors_total 0
The pattern is the same after the plain and proxy-ish GET /. Each time I scrape /metrics, it returns 200 and increments both sftpgo_http_req_total and sftpgo_http_req_ok_total. Each time I hit GET /, it returns 301 and increments sftpgo_http_req_total but does not increment the 2xx “ok” counter. That is why after each “GET / then scrape” step, req_total jumps by 2 while req_ok_total jumps by 1. This shows the counters move the same way for the same request regardless of whether I include forwarded headers, and it also shows the self-scrape effect of /metrics.

To answer whether the working directory affects the proxy logging story, I started SFTPGo from /tmp so it could not pick up the repo config from . and I saw the config loader warning that it was using defaults. Then I sent the same proxy-ish request again and captured the access log line. The config discovery behavior changed, but the proxy logging behavior I care about did not. The proxy request still logged remote_addr as 203.0.113.9 and the logged uri still started with http://.
{"level":"warn","sender":"config","message":"error loading configuration file: Unsupported Config Type \"\". Default configuration will be used: {...}"}{"level":"info","time":"[REDACTED]","sender":"httpd","method":"GET","proto":"HTTP/1.1","remote_addr":"203.0.113.9","request_id":"[REDACTED]","uri":"http://hosthdr.example/","user_agent":"curl/8.12.1","resp_status":301,"resp_size":45,"elapsed_ms":0}

I also tested two “forgiving” failure modes. When I ran with a valid DB file but I did not provide the templates directory in the temp config dir, the process crashed with a panic and exited non-zero.
EC=2panic: open /tmp/.../templates/base.html: no such file or directory

When I held the default SFTP port open and ran SFTPGo, it logged a bind error and said it could not start the SFTP server, but it still exited zero and it still created id_rsa in the temp config dir.
EC=0{"level":"warn","sender":"sftpd","message":"error starting listener on address :2022: listen tcp :2022: bind: address already in use"}{"level":"error","sender":"service","message":"could not start SFTP server: listen tcp :2022: bind: address already in use"}
After I gathered the evidence, I stopped SFTPGo, removed the temporary config directories and temporary files I created for testing, and I did not modify any repository source files.
